conclusion: On reviewed Chromium main, Fetch.continueRequest cannot legally inject Proxy-Authorization: explicit unsafe-header validation rejects Proxy-* case-insensitively. verified_facts.fact: Both fixed/group actual browser runners set Proxy-Authorization and Authorization using Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders immediately before Page.navigate.

Browser hosts require actual inbound synthetic Proxy-Authorization and origin Authorization; runner requires absent proxy header and preserved origin Authorization at the independent upstream peer. Removing the browser proxy header or injecting it in the host after ingress would not satisfy the existing witness.
Public CDP continueRequest.headers overrides request headers, does not automatically extend to redirects. Its schema does not promise every syntactically valid name is accepted.
Chromium NetworkHandler::SetExtraHTTPHeaders validates string type and header syntax, then records extra_request_headers; it does not call IsRequestHeaderSafe here.
network::IsRequestHeaderSafe rejects case-insensitive Proxy- prefix at lines113-115. Authorization is deliberately excluded from unsafe list.
FetchHandler::ContinueRequest calls ValidateHeadersForRequest for each header; unsafe header returns InvalidParams("Unsafe header: " + name) before applying modifications.
CorsURLLoaderFactory::IsValidRequest returns false for unsafe request.headers or cors_exempt_headers; CreateLoaderAndStart completes invalid request with net::ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.
